subject.title: fix(tlon): cap SSE payload JSON.parse at 16 MiB to prevent OOM

question: Is authenticated final-head Tlon connection, delivery, acknowledgement, and reconnect proof required before landing, or is the production-parser negative control plus focused boundary coverage sufficient?
rationale: The final code is well-covered in-process, but it adds an upstream-undefined hard ceiling and exercises a real channel lifecycle path that the contributor could not run; only the Tlon owner can accept the remaining proof and compatibility risk.

options.title: Require authenticated lifecycle proof
options.body: Obtain redacted final-head evidence for connection, normal subscription delivery, acknowledgement, oversized rejection, and reconnect/resubscription before merge.

options.title: Accept parser-level proof
options.body: Land based on the production-method negative control and boundary tests while explicitly accepting the OpenClaw-owned ceiling and skipped oversized events.

options.title: Wait for a Tlon environment
options.body: Keep the PR open until a suitable authenticated ship is available rather than lowering the proof requirement.

recommendation.title: Require authenticated lifecycle proof
recommendation.body: Obtain redacted final-head evidence for connection, normal subscription delivery, acknowledgement, oversized rejection, and reconnect/resubscription before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: The live assignee authored the final semantic refinements and is the strongest available owner for accepting or requiring lifecycle proof.
